title: Similar Figures
short: Figures are similar if rigid motions and a dilation map one to the other.

blocks.html: Congruent figures match exactly. Similar figures have the same shape but may differ in size. Dilations make the difference.

A dilation multiplies every length by the same factor $k$ and keeps every angle. Rigid motions then move the scaled copy into place without changing anything. So in similar figures, corresponding angles are equal and every pair of corresponding sides has the same ratio, $k$.

Two figures are similar if a dilation together with rigid motions maps one onto the other. Then corresponding angles are equal and corresponding sides are proportional: $$\frac{\text{side in the image}}{\text{matching side in the original}} = k$$

blocks.name: transform
blocks.cap: A dilation by 1.5. Add a slide, flip or turn: the image stays similar.

blocks.title: Are they similar?
blocks.q: Is a 4 by 6 rectangle similar to a 6 by 9 rectangle? To a 5 by 7 rectangle?
steps: $\frac{6}{4} = 1.5$ and $\frac{9}{6} = 1.5$: the same factor, so yes.

blocks.title: Angles carry over
blocks.q: $\triangle ABC \sim \triangle DEF$ with $\angle A = 50^\circ$ and $\angle B = 60^\circ$. Find $\angle F$.
steps: Corresponding angles are equal: $\angle D = 50^\circ$, $\angle E = 60^\circ$.

blocks.html: Adding instead of multiplying. Adding 2 to each side of a 4 by 6 rectangle gives 6 by 8, which is not similar: $\frac{6}{4} = 1.5$ but $\frac{8}{6} \approx 1.33$. Similar figures scale every length by the same factor.
